humanities_role_explanation: Historical 16th-century Latin and Early New High German letters (Bullinger correspondence) supply the texts, but the competence tested is general machine translation and summarization quality, not disciplinary scholarship.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only: Latin and ENH-German letter text translated or summarized into modern English and German.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Machine translation of Latin into German and English (BLEU/ChrF against a human reference translation), and cross-language paragraph-wise summarization of Latin and ENH-German letters into English and German, evaluated against expert-written summaries and manual judgement of names, times & events, completeness, correctness.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to MT and summarization of one historical letter corpus; not a broad multi-task benchmark, and no benchmark is introduced.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: GPT-4 is evaluated, compared with Google Translate, LingvaNex, Yandex, ModernMT, Niutrans and DeepL.

quantitative_metrics.note: BLEU, ChrF, and manual evaluator scores out of 58 paragraphs.

summary: The paper evaluates GPT-4 for machine translation of 16th-century Latin letters into German and English and compares it to online MT systems. It also tests GPT-4 for paragraph-wise cross-language summarization of Latin and Early New High German letters against expert-written summaries, using BLEU and manual evaluation.
key_findings: GPT-4 reaches BLEU 27.07 (Latin to German) and 34.50 (Latin to English) on the 121-sentence test set, versus Google Translate 17.53 and 25.22. Against human summaries BLEU is low (4.93 for MT; 6.23 for Latin summaries into German), but manual evaluation scored names 47.2/58, times & events 54.5/58, completeness 48.2/58, correctness 43.5/58, with no hallucinations noted.
evaluation_unit: Latin sentence (test set of 8 letters); the summarization experiment uses 10 Latin and 10 ENH-German letters (58 paragraphs manually judged)
gold_upstream: Test set of Fischer et al. (2022): 8 letters manually translated into German by a domain expert; English references obtained by translating the German with GPT-4.
facets_explanation: The MT test set comes from Fischer et al. (2022) and its German references were manually translated by a domain expert; English references were machine-translated from German by GPT-4. Summarization references are expert-written summaries from the Bullinger edition, and manual evaluation was done by three annotators. BLEU/ChrF scoring compares against a single reference.
results_explanation: Table 1: GPT-4 27.07 BLEU (Latin to German) and 34.50 BLEU (Latin to English), versus Google Translate 17.53 and 25.22. The same GPT-4 translations scored only 4.93 BLEU against human summaries as references instead of the real translation (a different reference type for the same task; 27.07 vs 4.93 is about 22 points, and 34.50 vs 6.80 is about 28 points for English), so the gap point value is a rough derived figure. No human baseline number is reported.

humanities_role.quote: We tested multilingual Large Language Models, in particular GPT-4, on letters from the 16th century that are in Latin and Early New High German.

dataset_size.quote: These 8 letters sum up to a total of 121 Latin sentences

evaluation_set_size.quote: BLEU and ChrF scores when translating the Latin test set (121 sentences) into German and English.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: we fed the complete test set to GPT-4 with a single prompt: “Translate the following text from Latin into L”

gold_source.quote: We used the test set of Fischer et al. (2022) which consists of 8 letters which have been manually translated into German by a domain expert.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: GPT-4 knows a surprising number of Latin city names and translates them correctly into modern day equivalents

answer_multiplicity.quote: BLEU (Papineni et al., 2002) is a precision-oriented word n-gram overlap metric which is often used in MT evaluation.

gold_upstream_source.quote: manually translated into German by a domain expert

reported_format_gap.quote: With this setup GPT-4 achieved a low 4.93 BLEU points when we compare the automatic translation to the human summary in German.
GPT-4 reaching a BLEU score of 27.07 for Latin to German MT on the test set

reported_format_gap_points.quote: GPT-4 MT from Latin to English then results in 6.80 BLEU.
Google Translate reached a BLEU score of 25.22 for this language direction, while GPT-4 again betters it considerably, reaching 34.50.

reported_format_gap_kind.quote: we hypothesized that the summaries could be used as reference translations.

reported_best_score.quote: GPT-4 outperforms Google Translate on their test set
